ateret-zekenim/2:א: (1) Deaf — Bach wrote deaf l'chatchila does not fulfill, b'dieved fulfills; idiot and minor even b'dieved do not discharge others; all agree even a minor who reached chinuch does not discharge even b'dieved.
beer-hagolah/2:ג: (3) There — and Tanna Kama, but women discharge for men — Tur in name of Rashi Arakhin.
beur-hagra/1:ב: (2) Freed [slaves]. Rambam: even though he holds women are obligated and discharge because they were in that miracle, not so slaves who are exempt since they were not etc.; and there is a dispute for women here, not like Tur and Magen Avraham.
chokhmat-shlomo/1:_: Seif 5: if all know, each reads for himself. NB see Magen Avraham s.k. 10 who brought views whether another can discharge a friend in Megillah with fewer than ten — see there. At first glance difficult: why does the gemara in Megillah challenge from Megillah in its time individually, not in time with ten, from baraita 15th on Shabbat — see there "their time" — not that not-in-time is in-time; what is their time individually, also not-in-time individually? Perhaps say baraita deals whether individual can read alone — not-in-time like in-time, even not-in-time individual reads; Rav deals whether individual discharges another — says in its time read individually to discharge another too with one; language of R' Yehuda Azulai Magen Avraham cites: individual discharges another; so in many places among poskim and Rosh Hashanah laws — therefore said in its time even individually; but not-in-time requires discharging another with ten — why challenge? Must prove Megillah requires ten. At first could deflect per what seems to me: poskim's dispute depends gemara dispute why we don't say Hallel on Purim — one said still doing Achashverosh, one said this reading is its Hallel; per latter like prayer therefore ten fitting — explicit Magen Avraham Rosh Chodesh laws s.v. Badah brought proof Hallel from Mishnah dealing prayer law — see there; per former not like prayer therefore no ten — thus view not requiring ten holds like those who say they did four and Pharaoh didn't etc.; other requiring ten holds like "this reading is its Hallel" — therefore requires ten. Accordingly it fits in its time since obligated for Hallel therefore this replaces Hallel and needs ten; not-in-time no Hallel connection since drinking, joy, all Purim laws only in its time; early reading only remembrance and publicity — certainly no ten here; cannot say not-in-time with ten means one discharges another with ten — must mean he himself doesn't fulfill except with ten. Yet can prove requiring ten doesn't help women and children — Magen Avraham doubts; per above can prove doesn't help — if helped, gemara could reverse Rav's not-in-time with ten means he doesn't fulfill with fewer than ten; Tanna Erev Purim "their time" opposite — not like Yom Kippur no ten since no Hallel connection when not miracle day; Erev since still miracle day one doesn't discharge except with ten — why challenge? Actually challenges well: if not-in-time with ten, anyway needs ten even reading alone, kal vachomer discharging; what does Erev "their time" teach? Perhaps say for this ten of not-in-time women and children combine but discharging another if matter of kedusha needs ten adult men — therefore thought since not-in-time no Hallel, needs ten — women and children suffice; therefore teaches Erev "their time" since miracle day and need discharge with ten, must be adult males; Rav holds like R' Nachman this reading is Hallel — wouldn't challenge from Erev; since doesn't answer so, women and children never help — always need adults and males — clear without doubt.
eliyah-rabbah/2:_: [2] [Levush] that it is not strong etc. In Shulchan Aruch he wrote two views on this and Olat Shabbat wrote against his inclination he holds one does not discharge, for if not it would be difficult why he ruled seif 3 tumtum even of its kind does not discharge because of doubt — but even women discharge, until here. And it is puzzling, for Beit Yosef explicitly wrote that even per Rashi women discharge for men, nevertheless tumtum even of its kind does not discharge because it is a recognizable matter requiring investigation. And in any case for law, primary is like Levush and so Rama and poskim wrote, and see siman 471 seif 6 what I wrote to distinguish between Chanukah candle where they discharge and Megillah. It also appears to me Megillah is different, for she is not obligated in reading like men but in hearing, which is not so Chanukah candle — women and men are equal in the mitzvah.
kaf-hachayyim/2:_: b) There. And women — that they too were in that miracle. Megillah 4a. And meaning: even though Megillah reading comes from time to time and a time-caused obligation [women are generally exempt], as written in Kiddushin 29a, nevertheless here they are obligated since they too were in that miracle as written in scripture "children and women on one day." However there are commentators that "they too were in that miracle" means the miracle was done through a woman as Beit Yosef wrote. And see below letter 5.
levushei-serad/5:_: seif 4 and etc. — see there seif 3 and what Magen Avraham wrote that Rabbi [held] etc., meaning he brought at least a view that validates; and here he did not bring at all only the disqualifying, or in Beit Yosef there it implies he agreed so — see there. And Semag cites in the name of Rabbeinu Avraham — see there.
mishnah-berurah/2:ג: (ג) Or a minor — even though a minor is obligated at least rabbinically as above seif 1, nevertheless he cannot discharge an adult because regarding a minor it is two rabbinic levels (the reading itself is only rabbinic and the minor's obligation is also only rabbinic in all mitzvot), unlike an adult who is one rabbinic and one does not extract another rabbinic. Above siman 475:3 Mechaber brought some permit a minor who reached chinuch to discharge others in his lighting — same for Megillah; see Ikarei Dinim in name of Sema: in pressing need when no men expert in Megillah reading, a minor who reached chinuch may discharge them.
mishnah-berurah/2:ב: (5) Deaf — meaning one who speaks and does not hear at all; and even though generally we rule if he did not make heard to his ear he fulfilled as above siman 62 and siman 185, here regarding Megillah which is because of publicizing the miracle they were stricter — hearing in his ear is required, or because deaf is worse since he cannot make heard to his ear; and see Shaarei Teshuvah that specifically if he is completely deaf who does not hear at all — excluding if he hears when spoken to loudly. And all this is Shulchan Aruch's view; but many acharonim hold even if completely deaf, the listener fulfills from him; and nevertheless l'chatchila all agree they do not establish him to discharge the many. And know that one whose ears are damaged or who is far from the bimah and cannot hear well from the reader should be careful to read for himself from a kosher Megillah, or at least hold a chumash and the words he lacks say immediately from the chumash.
mishnah-berurah/6:ד: (19) Megillah reading — and now it is fitting for each to have a kosher Megillah and read word by word quietly, for impossible to hear from the shaliach tzibbur because of noise and confusion when they beat on wood and make sound; and fitting for all Israel who has ability [Peri Megadim]; and see below siman 690 seif 4.
peri-megadim/1:ב: (2) And accordingly we have a new law in Beit HaMikdash and the like that one blesses and others hear and fulfill — but a deaf person who speaks and does not hear cannot bless; and in gemara Berachos it implies other mitzvot are derived from Shema, and Rav Yosef alone holds the dispute is in Shema and in other mitzvot likewise one fulfills; and per Rav Yosef the Mishnah of Megillah — or they are separate — deaf l'chatchila no and minor b'dieved no; or deaf is different for he is not fit for hearing as Taz wrote (siman 353 and 695 regarding shaliach tzibbur — requires study). And Eliyah Rabbah ch. 4 siman 23: all obligated in Megillah are obligated in Chanukah — but there is a deaf person who does not hear who is exempt in Megillah and obligated in Chanukah; apparently difficult per what Taz wrote that in conclusion the Mishnah is R' Yehuda — why did he rule minor does not discharge adult per Tanna Kama of R' Yosi, for in conclusion all is R' Yosi and two types of minor — opening without reaching chinuch and when reached chinuch he does not disagree that he discharges adult; rather must rule as gemara initially that Mishnah is R' Yosi and R' Yehuda argues on minor, and that he does not argue on deaf — one can say deaf l'chatchila no; and on this Peri Megadim ch. 1 from Megillah and in Eliyah Rabbah Berachos 15 see there — if so, apparently difficult. And one can say gemara Shabbat 23a one who lit Chanukah lights does not help a woman — certainly she lights, and that is to discharge others; and from the anonymous [Mishnah] minor does not imply even one who reached chinuch — therefore ruled in Megillah likewise as anonymous of the Talmud. And the Mechaber in siman 475 appears from his words he rules like Baal HaItur that one who reached chinuch discharges (Magen Avraham letter 4) — one can say he goes to his view as Beit Yosef wrote here who distinguished between deaf of Megillah publicizing miracle and Mishnah opening not like R' Yosi and ruled like Tanna Kama as we said.
peri-megadim/1:ד: (4) And incidentally I saw to mention what Eliyah Rabbah wrote siman 62 in name of Maharam Alshkar: if one discharges his friend in Shema — speech is required, and it is difficult from Megillah to Beit HaGadol that women do not discharge men — these are by hearing and these by reading; and nevertheless all are fit to read Megillah and one discharges many; and Abudraham there is difficult. But per the conclusion there — shaliach tzibbur with ten discharges another (and there it is said one who answers amen is like one who says — and it is difficult what relevance answering amen has to Shema, and strained to say amen on blessings before and after is like he said Shema) — the same for Megillah that they bless before and after. And Magen Avraham letter 10 — see what Mechaber wrote: ten do not read except each for himself — because whenever there is no ten, one does not discharge his friend because reading is required; and he rules like Beit HaGadol women do not discharge men — women specifically in reading, and proof he did not write seif 2 in view one the reverse in view two as Magen Avraham wrote and in general Orach Chayyim in Pri Megadim 14 — requires study. See Pri Chadash wrote and it was explained that if he read and did not make heard to his ear he fulfilled. And it is difficult what he informs us — again I saw Shelah as Beit Yosef wrote to distinguish Megillah publicizing miracle and Taz deaf is different — and accordingly requires study in this law. Further one can say if we say in Megillah hearing is primary and there is a dispute for Shema "and you shall speak them" — speech is primary; and why there one does not discharge his friend — therefore R' Yosi holds there if he did not make heard to his ear he fulfilled, not so Megillah where hearing is primary — and see above in name of Eliyah Rabbah siman 62 — requires study. In name of the late R' [author] I found a deaf woman does not discharge other women — for this case, and per his view she is not obligated in the matter — we read for her that essence is hearing like deaf with shofar.
turei-zahav/2:_: If the reader was deaf etc. — Mishnah: all are fit to read Megillah except deaf-mute etc.; R' Yehuda permits a minor; who taught deaf unfit even b'dieved? R' Yehuda, since we teach: one who reads Shema and did not make it heard to his ear etc. until now that we come to this etc.; see what Beit Yosef wondered — truly a great difficulty: whatever you answer to be strict on deaf in Megillah is difficult why establish Mishnah as R' Yosi when even R' Yosi agrees here deaf forbidden — it appears all is fine: certainly deaf is worse than one who can hear but didn't make heard to his ear — he is at least fit to hear unlike deaf; per Chazal "all fit for mixing" etc.; therefore at the beginning we explain R' Yehuda and R' Yosi — R' Yehuda even l'chatchila fit in Shema since he doesn't require "hear" at all as in chapter "he was reading" — R' Yehuda derives Shema in any language you hear; no lesson from lack of hearing — likewise deaf; therefore forced to establish Mishnah as R' Yosi who disqualifies even without making heard, kal vachomer deaf here; end we establish Mishnah as R' Yehuda per Raavad who said must make heard to his ear — difficult in his words since "must" implies l'chatchila as Rashi; then brings verse implying even b'dieved since verse didn't mention l'chatchila — verse excludes only totally unfit to hear, i.e. deaf not fit to hear; but one fit to hear, lack of making heard doesn't prevent — only l'chatchila warning; therefore our Mishnah disqualifying deaf for Tanna Kama even per R' Yehuda — deaf is different; gemara didn't initially distinguish deaf from not making heard because they thought R' Yehuda doesn't require derasha "make heard to your ear"; we needn't distinguish fit to hear or not; if we want to distinguish saying from reason there is inferiority in lack of hearing — cannot distinguish deaf from not making heard; therefore as challenged initially — perhaps R' Yehuda, l'chatchila forbidden — then wouldn't distinguish deaf from not making heard except both l'chatchila forbidden — then we'd know no verse; in conclusion they derive from verse inferiority of lack of hearing and verse certainly disqualifies even b'dieved — plain disqualification except Tanna said l'chatchila language but b'dieved not — therefore we must distinguish: verse speaks of deaf disqualified b'dieved since not fit to hear at all; Tanna's l'chatchila language speaks of not making heard — all fit for mixing etc.; therefore our Mishnah on deaf even b'dieved disqualifies even per R' Yehuda; though derasha in conclusion Mishnah also l'chatchila only, poskim don't accept — no l'chatchila distinction except not making heard; deaf disqualified even b'dieved — clear and bright without doubt.
shaarei-teshuvah/2:_: Did not fulfill. Av Beit HaTefillah; see Shevut Yaakov vol. 3 siman 33 who wrote there it is difficult to be lenient like Bach against the meaning of the rishonim; and see there he wrote in (1) that they honored his ears from hearing unless they shout very loudly — then he hears; and he read the Megillah before the congregation in a medium voice — it seems he himself did not make it heard to his ear; nevertheless the congregation fulfilled with this reading, for complete deafness is not the case since he hears if they shout as Rash wrote in responsum kelal 85 siman 12 and in simanim there and in Peri Chadash Orach Chayyim Gitin siman 121 who wrote that even if he does not hear except when spoken to in a loud voice through some kind of trumpets and the like — nevertheless he is not called deaf; also one need not be concerned because he did not make heard to his ear, since it is evident from the dispute of poskim from Shema to Megillah as explained in Beit Yosef that there is a difference between not making heard to one's ear and deaf (and what Beit Yosef and Bach wrote is very strained); and it appears specifically a deaf person who is not fit to make heard to his ear — since he heard from his mouth he is not obligated in reading he did not fulfill; unlike this one who can hear through loud voice and is obligated in his reading — also listeners from him in medium voice fulfilled — see there. And it appears he himself too one may say fulfilled even though he did not make heard to his ear, for nevertheless he is fit to read; and since he himself is the reader he fulfilled through his reading even though he did not make heard to his ear, like Shema where he read and did not make heard — he fulfilled; and reading is like hearing from others from him; and although others heard and he did not hear — nevertheless he fulfilled in reading he read for himself; see above siman 62.
